approach:
Add one new gate function, `jobs::provenance(git, change, judged, history)`, in crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs. It judges a job's records against the cross-links that Athena's own writers always leave. It is separate from `jobs::check`, so `jobs::check`, `job_records_of` and every existing landing test keep their present behavior. Every refusal is a `Rule::JobRecords` violation whose detail starts with the constant `jobs::PROVENANCE` ("provenance: ") and names the record path and the missing or contradicting evidence. The repair names the Athena command that writes the evidence.

The function fires in two cases.
- A commit adds a closing score (no `cause`) or any outcome of a request job. The check then covers:
  - (R1) For each reading of the job: a request record with `received_at <= reading.at`; a Reader invocation whose `seq == invocation_seq` and whose `ended_at <= reading.at`; a `base_commit` the repository holds; and a `defaults_sha256` equal to `sha256_hex(defaults.toml at base_commit)`. This is what refuses a hand-made proposal closed with `athena close` (forgery c).
  - (R2) When `job.json` exists: every dispatch field is present. The config and defaults hashes equal the accepted reading's. `base_commit` is held and its `defaults.toml` matches.
  - (R4) When the outcome is Landed: Producer and Verifier invocations start at or after `dispatched_at`. The named verifier invocation starts at or after every producer's `ended_at`. `outcome.at >= verifier.ended_at`. This is the contradiction test for a forged landing of a dispatched job that never closed (forgery b).
- A commit adds `job.json` but none of the job's candidate, verification or outcome files. (R3) The accepted reading must already be in the parent tree (`judged.base`), because Athena commits the reading first. This refuses records written in one batch across two commits (forgery a). A squash adds the closing records too, so it is exempt.

Where it runs (this answers findings 1 and 2).
- The live gate: `gate()` in lib.rs for Scope::CommitMsg, Scope::Commit and Scope::CommitLegacyUsage. That covers `athena close`, which calls `gate` from manage.rs:188-190, and the commit-msg hook.
- The history walk only when it is not frozen legacy. `check_history_with_exempt` becomes a thin wrapper over a private `walk(git, tip, exempt, provenance)` with `provenance = false`. So legacy.rs:192 (`check_legacy`) is byte-for-byte what it is today. `check_history` calls `walk(.., true)` only on the branch where the tip config has no `cutover_job` (history.rs:47-49).
- The pending-cutover and cutover-configured fall-backs (history.rs:55 and 63) stay frozen. Their commits become pre-C0 history.
- After C0: `check_after_cutover` also loops over `c0..tip` (`rev-list --reverse`) and runs `jobs::provenance` on each commit. A job written by hand on main after the cutover is therefore judged by CI.

Not covered, and stated as such: job records written only to the `athena/records` branch (own root, a different layout, with its audit checking only append-only). The docs and CHANGELOG say so, and an open question names the follow-up.

No record field is added, so records.rs and reconcile.rs stay untouched. Reconcile already checks outcome totals against invocation sums (reconcile.rs header). Tests go in the existing landing_tests.rs (new genuine-shaped helpers, old helpers untouched), plus one test each in history.rs and legacy.rs. The docs and CHANGELOG state what is detected and the residual: fully mimicked records pass, forgery (b) is caught only when its times or fields contradict the dispatch, and nothing is signed.

decisions.choice: Make the provenance check a separate pub function `jobs::provenance`, called from `gate()` (Scope::CommitMsg, Scope::Commit, Scope::CommitLegacyUsage) and from the non-legacy history walk. Do not put it inside `jobs::check`.
decisions.reason: `jobs::check` is reached from the frozen legacy walk (legacy.rs:192 -> check_history_with_exempt -> history.rs:255) with `history = Some(..)`. Putting the new rules there would re-judge pre-C0 genuine records that may lack dispatch fields (every dispatch field on `Job` is an Option, records.rs:607-620). The exempt list at that path comes from legacy-exempt.json and cannot grow (records-history.md section 4). A separate function lets each caller choose. It also leaves `job_records_of`, which calls `jobs::check`, and every existing landing test as they are (finding 4).

rejected.option: Run the checks inside `jobs::check` for every history (the round-1 design)
rejected.why: Re-judges frozen pre-C0 history and offers no usable remedy there (critic finding 1).
Needs an edit to invariant.rs for no gain. A private `walk(.., provenance: bool)` parameter in history.rs carries the same switch.
A forger picks an old id.

decisions.choice: The history walk applies provenance only when the tip config has no `cutover_job`. The frozen/pending/not-shown branches pass `false`. After the cutover is shown, `check_after_cutover` runs provenance over the commits `c0..tip`.
decisions.reason: Pre-C0 main cannot gain commits, so nothing is lost by freezing it. Commits after C0 are not judged by `jobs::check` today (check_after_cutover uses classify_pre_merge, attribution and reconcile only), so without the new loop a hand-written job on main after C0 would only meet the commit-time hook, which a person can skip. The loop reuses the same function, with no exemption needed (history = None).

rejected.option: Narrow the claim to commit time only after C0
rejected.why: Weaker than a cheap loop that exists. Kept as the stated residual for the records branch only.

That branch has a root-level layout and its only audit is append-only (records_branch.rs audit_commits). The run of the check on it needs a layout adapter and a fixture, which is a separate job; see open question.

decisions.choice: No new record field. records.rs and reconcile.rs are listed as expected deliverables but are not touched.
decisions.reason: Every link used is written today: reading `base_commit` / `defaults_sha256` / `invocation_seq` (reading.rs:788-796), the request record, and the dispatch fields of job.json (run/mod.rs:952-991). A stamped witness field is a value a forger recomputes and adds allow-list surface for no assurance. Criterion 7 then holds because nothing new is stored.

rejected.option: A chain hash or witness field on Score or Outcome
rejected.why: Recomputable by the forger; real signing is out of scope.

rejected.option: Link forgery (b) through the verifier invocation's `InvocationContext` hashes (records.rs:658-664)
rejected.why: I read the struct. Its hashes are values the writer chooses, so they bind nothing a forger cannot invent. Verification.verified_fingerprint is already compared by the landing invariant.

decisions.choice: `defaults_sha256` is recomputed from `defaults.toml` at the reading's `base_commit`. `config_sha256` is only compared between job.json and the accepted reading, never recomputed.
decisions.reason: `defaults_sha256` is `sha256_hex(defaults.toml bytes at commit)` (capability.rs:38-51), so it recomputes exactly in any later build. `config_sha256` hashes `Config::reading_inputs()` (capability.rs:45), which follows the code of the build that wrote it; recomputing would falsely refuse old genuine readings. Dispatch itself forces job and reading hashes to be equal (run/mod.rs:798).

rejected.option: Recompute `config_sha256` from athena.toml at the base
rejected.why: A later change to `reading_inputs` or the config schema would refuse genuine records.

decisions.choice: A missing dispatch or reading field is a refusal on the live and non-legacy paths, with no leniency for null.
decisions.reason: The old hand-written fixture shape is all-null (landing_tests.rs `job_record`); leniency on null would let the forger omit the field. Old genuine commits are protected by the frozen legacy path, not by leniency.

rejected.option: Require fields only when `dispatch_branch` is present

decisions.choice: Judge commit order per commit (job.json added without closing records needs the accepted reading in `judged.base`), with no new state in HistoryState.
decisions.reason: Athena commits the reading before dispatch (the Dispatch commit message in run/mod.rs says so). The parent tree shows the order, so the hook, the pre-merge gate and the CI walk all give the same verdict. Step 1 re-confirms in reading.rs and run/mod.rs that no genuine writer puts reading and job.json in one commit.

rejected.option: Compare record timestamps with commit dates
rejected.why: A squash or rebase makes commit dates arbitrary.
Helps only the CI walk, not the hook.

decisions.choice: Forgery (b) is detected only through its contradictions with the dispatch (missing dispatch fields, producer or verifier before `dispatched_at`, verifier before producers ended, outcome before verifier end, base or defaults mismatch). The docs and CHANGELOG say exactly that and call it the weakest of the three.
decisions.reason: Finding 3: a (b) forgery whose times reconcile still passes; I found no committed value that a forger cannot compute alone. Saying so plainly is more useful than a stronger claim.

decisions.choice: Existing tests keep their old fixtures. `landing_tests.rs::history_of` is changed to call `check_history_with_exempt(git, "HEAD", None)` (the frozen judgment it exercised before), and history.rs:317 does the same. New tests use new genuine-shaped helpers and new `provenance_of` / `provenance_history_of` helpers.
decisions.reason: Finding 4: the fixture migration of round 1 touched `opening` at every call site. The grep shows the exact-equality callers are `history_of` (12 sites in landing_tests.rs) and history.rs:317. The CLI suites use real writers, which are genuine. athena-cli reconcile.rs and labeled.rs build outcomes but go through attribution/status, not `check_history`, so they are unaffected.

rejected.option: Migrate `opening` and all call sites to genuine shape
rejected.why: Open-ended and not needed once provenance is a separate function.

This plan adds no parser, stem list, stop list or reading check. The input forms are record shapes, mapped to the new tests: whole job by hand (test a), forged landing (test b), hand-made proposal (test c), genuine records (test d). The producer and verifier still run `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` as a no-regression command; I cite no case ids and no result.

rejected.option: Add corpus cases for forged record shapes
rejected.why: The corpus runs request text, not commit records.

demonstrations.method:
Run the athena-gate test suite. New tests in landing_tests.rs (a, b, c, d) build real temporary git repositories and assert Violations from `jobs::provenance` and from the history walk. One new test in history.rs and one in legacy.rs cover the post-C0 and pre-C0 paths. Fixtures use the new genuine-shaped helpers.
(a) `a_job_written_by_hand_across_two_commits_is_refused`: commit 1 adds the old all-null `opening(&HONEST)` (reading, job.json, reader invocation); commit 2 adds the hand change plus `closing(fp)`. A second variant has full genuine evidence but the reading and job.json in the same commit.
(b) `a_forged_landing_of_a_dispatched_job_that_never_closed_is_refused`: a genuine Read commit and Dispatch commit, then one forged commit with the change and closing records. Variants, each breaking one link: producer started before `dispatched_at`; verifier started before the producer ended; outcome before the verifier ended; a dispatch field missing; the job's defaults hash differing from the reading's. A control with consistent times is accepted.
(c) `a_hand_made_proposal_closed_with_athena_close_is_refused`: a reading with invented forecasts and no request or reader invocation, closed by the records `manage.rs::close_with` writes (a closing score from `jobs::expected_score` and a Dropped outcome). The same proposal with a request record, a reader invocation, a held base commit and a matching defaults hash is accepted. The refused commit is also run through `crate::gate(.., Scope::CommitMsg)` to show the wiring.
(d) `a_genuine_landing_is_not_refused` (see criterion 3).
history.rs: `provenance_is_judged_on_main_commits_after_c0` builds the existing cutover `world(true)` with `record_cutover`, adds a commit on top that holds hand-made job records, and asserts a violation with the provenance prefix at that commit. legacy.rs: `a_pre_c0_commit_with_old_shape_job_records_gets_no_provenance_finding` gives the same violations as `check_history_with_exempt(.., Some(vec![]))` (the comparison at legacy.rs:304) and none starts with the provenance prefix.
demonstrations.observes: Each forged history gives at least one `Rule::JobRecords` violation whose detail begins `provenance: ` and names the evidence.
